steps.title: Gather reagents and materials
steps.instruction: Collect snap‑frozen human skeletal muscle biopsies and the following reagents with their catalog numbers and working dilutions: anti‑human CD31‑Alexa Fluor® 594 (1:400, BioLegend 303126), rabbit anti‑laminin (1:2000, Sigma‑Aldrich L9393), goat anti‑rabbit Alexa Fluor® 750 (1:1000, Thermo Fisher A21039), optional anti‑human CD105‑biotin (1:100, BioLegend 323214), Streptavidin‑Alexa Fluor® 647 (1:500, Life Technologies S21374), OCT embedding matrix (VWR 361603E), NaCl, Na₂HPO₄·2H₂O, KCl, KH₂PO₄, Tween‑20, skim milk powder, DAPI (1:1000 dilution, Sigma‑Aldrich 28718‑90‑3), ProLong™ Gold antifade mountant (ThermoFisher P10144), nail polish, SuperFrost slides, immunopen, and a cryostat.

steps.title: Prepare buffer solutions
steps.instruction: Make the following solutions: PBS 10× by dissolving 80 g NaCl, 15 g Na₂HPO₄·2H₂O, 2 g KCl, and 1.2 g KH₂PO₄ in distilled water and bring to 1 L; dilute to 1× for use. Prepare PBST (0.05 % Tween‑20) by mixing 0.5 mL Tween‑20 with 999.5 mL 1× PBS. Prepare PBST + 5 % milk by adding 2.5 mg skim‑milk powder to 50 mL PBST.

steps.title: Cryosection muscle biopsies
steps.instruction: Clean equipment, set cryostat temperature as required, equilibrate biopsies inside the cryostat, embed each biopsy in Tissue‑Tek OCT, mount on specimen holders, cut sections of 10–16 µm thickness onto SuperFrost slides, and store slides at –20 °C or –80 °C until staining.

steps.title: Air‑dry and outline sections
steps.instruction: Remove slides from –20 °C storage, air‑dry at room temperature for 30 min, then draw an outline around each tissue section with an immunopen placed 2–3 mm from the tissue edge to limit antibody volume.

steps.title: Block non‑specific binding
steps.instruction: Cover each section with ~40 µL PBST + 5 % milk, incubate 30 min at room temperature, then wash three times with ~40 µL PBST for 5 min each.

steps.title: Primary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Prepare an antibody mix in PBST containing anti‑human CD31‑Alexa 594, rabbit anti‑laminin, and optional anti‑human CD105‑biotin at the dilutions listed above. Apply 20 µL to each section, incubate 2 h at room temperature in the dark, then wash three times with a large volume of PBST (≈40 µL) for 5 min each.

steps.title: Secondary antibody incubation
steps.instruction: Prepare a secondary mix in PBST with goat anti‑rabbit Alexa 750 (to detect laminin) and optional Streptavidin‑Alexa 647 (to detect CD105). Apply 20 µL to each section, incubate 1 h at room temperature in the dark, then wash three times with a large volume of PBST for 5 min each.

steps.title: DAPI nuclear counterstain
steps.instruction: Dilute DAPI 1:1000 in PBST, apply ~20 µL to each section, incubate 5–10 min in the dark, gently rinse with PBST to remove excess dye.

steps.title: Mount slides
steps.instruction: Add ~10 µL ProLong™ Gold antifade mountant to each section, place a coverslip, seal edges with nail polish while avoiding air bubbles, let cure 24 h at room temperature in the dark, then store slides at 4 °C (up to 1 month; imaging preferably within a week).

steps.title: Acquire fluorescence images
steps.instruction: Using a Zeiss Axio Scan.Z1 slide scanner with ZEN 2 software, set the 10×/0.45 Plan‑Apochromat objective and single‑band filter excitation ranges: DAPI 335–355 nm, CD31‑Alexa 594 574–599 nm, CD105‑Alexa 647 650–670 nm (optional), Laminin‑Alexa 750 672–747 nm. Optimize exposure and intensity on a test slide for each channel, enable stitching for high‑throughput acquisition, and keep all acquisition settings identical for all slides and batches.

steps.title: Laminin segmentation (ImageJ)
steps.instruction: Run ImageJ/Fiji macros 2–4 (available on GitHub) on the acquired images; macros 2, 4 run automatically, macro 3 may require manual adjustment as described. Save intermediate mask images in a folder named “check” and area‑reporting .txt files in a folder named “ROI”.

steps.title: CD31/CD105 segmentation and quantification
steps.instruction: Run ImageJ/Fiji macro 6 on the same images: apply Gaussian blur, threshold with the “Li dark” algorithm, perform Watershed separation, Fill Holes, overlay the laminin mask to create a capillary mask, then measure mean fluorescence intensity, area, and circularity for CD31 and CD105 objects. Save results in a folder named “segmentation”. (Batch files on GitHub can automate these steps.)

steps.title: Quantify capillary density in R
steps.instruction: Open the provided R Markdown file in RStudio. Execute the following code chunks in order: (1) “myofibersTotalArea” to consolidate myofiber data, count objects per sample, compute total myofiber area, keep the replicate with the most myofibers, and discard samples with <100 myofibers; (2) “positiveCD31Area” to consolidate CD31 (and optional CD105) quantification and plot the proportion of CD31‑positive area per sample; (3) “capillaryDensity” to filter capillary objects (positive for both CD31 and CD105, size 3–51 µm², circularity >0.5), compute and plot capillary density as number of capillaries per µm² of total myofiber area (alternatively per myofiber).
